paths.description: Homepage and discovery hub, representing the main acquisition, game-discovery, consent and registration entry experience.
Promotions listing, representing regulated commercial offers and campaign cards.
Casino listing, representing the primary game-discovery catalogue.
Sportsbook, representing the live-data betting journey and network-dependent state handling.
Help centre, representing support and recovery content.
Registration entry flow inspected through the first personal-data form; no personal data was submitted.
Synthetic missing route used to inspect HTTP failure handling and indexing policy.

findings.summary: The site exposes only a hard-coded dark palette rather than following the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The normal and emulated-dark screenshots are visually identical, and the computed root color-scheme is not declared as a light/dark pair.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not stop non-essential motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, 13 animations remained, including continuously running blink animations at 800 ms and 1000 ms and ten 350 ms row-slide animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes blinking, row entrance motion and non-essential transitions.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found browser support but no view-transition CSS or authored transition names across the representative Next.js UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use document.startViewTransition for same-document state changes and cross-document view-transition CSS for route changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The cookie consent panel obscures primary content on every sampled mobile route.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots of home, promotions, casino, sports and help show the same large fixed consent panel covering roughly the lower quarter to third of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally permissible, keep equivalent accept/reject choices visible, and preserve access to the current task.

findings.summary: Modal overlays are implemented as custom divs rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero dialog and zero popover elements; the registration overlay is a div with role=dialog and the consent surface has no dialog semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal account flows and popover for transient UI, including native focus management and light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: The first viewport is crowded with rankings, live win amounts, carousels and persistent chrome.
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage shows header, hero, paid-today carousel, bettor ranking, search, content tabs, bottom navigation and consent at once, leaving little stable task space.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneous promotional modules, prioritize one primary task, and defer secondary live rankings below the first viewport.

findings.summary: Several primary touch targets are shorter than the recommended target size.
findings.evidence: The platform probe measured the visible Cadastre-se control at 34 px high and Entrar at 38 px high, below a comfortable 44 px target.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44 CSS px without relying on visual size alone and retain the visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: The sportsbook converts failed live-data requests into a misleading empty state with no retry.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence records repeated 403/ERR_FAILED responses from prod20562.fssb.io while the sports page says “Nenhum evento encontrado” and offers no retry or failure explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Distinguish network/API failure from a genuine empty result, announce the state, and provide retry plus support/recovery paths.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.0 s, FCP 4.7 s, TBT 710 ms, CLS 0.155 and a performance score of 0.36; the raw-CDP trace corroborated LCP 2.79 s and 98.69 ms blocking time in a less-throttled run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce initial CSS/JS/font payloads, defer trackers and non-critical modules, then remeasure under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Late content causes visible layout instability.
findings.evidence: The 360 px layout observer measured CLS 0.131, dominated by a 0.1308 shift at about 5.3 s; the image audit found 16 images without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic image and dynamic-module space with width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid inserting late banners above settled content.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is oversized and fragmented.
findings.evidence: The HAR contains 295 requests and 4.09 MB transferred, including 29 stylesheets and 1.35 MB of fonts; numerous parser-inserted stylesheets are VeryHigh-priority render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and consolidate fonts, reduce critical CSS, preload only true critical resources and defer route-irrelevant styles and scripts.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused CSS and JavaScript ship on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 330 KiB unused JavaScript and 144 KiB unused CSS; FontAwesome all.css is 99.9% unused and analytics bundles dominate several waste entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split route features, replace full icon-font bundles with used SVGs/subsets, and load analytics only after valid consent.

findings.summary: Text and primary controls fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 19 contrast failures, including white Cadastre-se text on #ff9400 at 2.21:1 and ranking labels at 3.17:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and test every state in the dark theme.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is not consistently logical.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; DOM recon shows early H3 headings before the page H1, and the help route renders two H1 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Place one descriptive H1 near the start of each main region, follow sequential heading levels and add a semantic main landmark.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration prevents normal pinch zoom.
findings.evidence: The rendered viewport meta includes maximum-scale=1 even though the narrow layout itself has no horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and do not disable user scaling; retain the existing fluid no-overflow layout.

findings.summary: The page loads with browser console errors and runtime request failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 13 console-error items and a failed errors-in-console audit; HAR also records failed/aborted requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix first-party errors, handle expected third-party failures without uncaught noise, and enforce clean-console checks in CI.

findings.summary: Several images have incorrect aspect ratios or missing dimensions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 8 distorted image instances, while the image primitive found 16 missing-dimension and 15 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve intrinsic aspect ratios, declare dimensions and keep responsive srcset/sizes for content imagery.

findings.summary: Security policy coverage is incomplete and multiple cookies are insecure.
findings.evidence: CSP is limited to frame-ancestors, with no script-src/object-src; nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent. The cookie audit found 11 cookies with issues, including analytics cookies lacking Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies, and set Secure/SameSite appropriately on every cookie.

findings.summary: Tracking starts with a large third-party footprint before an affirmative consent choice.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR includes 87 third-party requests and 1.08 MB; the tracker probe found 16 third-party origins and DoubleClick, Facebook and Google Ads trackers while the consent panel was still shown.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics/advertising storage and requests until opt-in, minimize vendors and retention, and provide an equally prominent reject-all action.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only despite a relevant account flow.
findings.evidence: The registration form requests a password and the runtime/source probe found no PublicKeyCredential or navigator.credentials integration; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys/WebAuthn for sign-in and reauthentication while retaining a secure fallback.

findings.summary: The app manifest is present but no service worker is registered.
findings.evidence: The manifest declares standalone display and start_url, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned an empty list, so no offline fallback is available.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a scoped service worker and provide a purposeful offline shell/fallback for help and account-recovery content.

findings.summary: Consent does not offer an equivalent reject-all choice.
findings.evidence: The first layer offers Personalizar and a brightly emphasized Aceitar tudo. After Personalizar, visible actions are Salvar preferências and Aceitar tudo, still with no reject-all control.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept all and Reject all with equal prominence, use privacy-preserving defaults, and make withdrawal as easy as consent.

findings.summary: Registration disables or omits useful autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The email field uses autocomplete=off and the CPF field has no autocomplete token; only the password field has new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email, name and inputmode tokens appropriate to each field; do not disable password-manager/autofill support.

findings.summary: The responsible-gambling limit defaults to unlimited during account creation.
findings.evidence: The registration form visibly labels “Limites de Jogo Responsável” with “Ilimitado (padrão)” before account creation.
findings.suggestedFix: Require an explicit, informed limit choice, make protective limits easy to choose and change, and avoid unlimited as the preselected default.

findings.summary: Page weight and third-party resources are disproportionate to the first-view task.
findings.evidence: The initial page transfers 4.09 MB across 295 requests; 1.08 MB and 87 requests are third-party, with 1.35 MB in fonts alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level byte/request budgets, defer non-essential trackers, subset fonts and avoid loading offscreen live modules before demand.

findings.summary: The homepage has a high baseline memory footprint for a discovery page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 939,206 heap nodes and 54.4 MB self size with 3,325 DOM elements; repeated filter toggling did not grow it further, but the initial footprint is heavy.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneously mounted hidden desktop/mobile trees, virtualize repeated cards and dispose unused live-data objects and subscriptions.

taskList.title: Gate trackers on valid consent and add a symmetric reject-all action
Cut the critical payload and fix LCP/CLS
Fix contrast, heading order, zoom and target sizes
Harden CSP, headers and cookie attributes
Expose honest sportsbook failure and retry states
Replace custom modal surfaces with semantic primitives
Add preference-aware theming and reduced-motion rules
Add offline fallback and passkey support
